My Life, My Rhythm

Talking about yourself, your routines and what's happening in your life right now. Lots of talking, step by step, with phrases that help you when you get stuck.

Reading: Confessions of a Night Owl

10 min

Before you read

Look at the title: Confessions of a Night Owl. What do you think a night owl's day is like? Guess three things, then read and check.

Confessions of a Night Owl

a blog post by Lily, 29

Hi, I'm Lily, and I'm a night owl. My friends are usually in bed by eleven, but I rarely go to sleep before two. I'm not lazy. My brain just works better at night!

On weekdays I work from home, so I don't need to get up early. I usually wake up at around ten, grab a coffee and check my emails. In the afternoon I run errands or meet friends. My most productive time starts at about 9 p.m. That's when I write, plan and get creative.

At the weekend I take it easy. I sleep in, I catch up with friends and sometimes I binge-watch a good series.

This month, though, things are different. I'm learning Spanish because I'm going to Madrid in the summer, so I'm trying to go to bed earlier and study in the mornings. It's really hard! Right now, as I'm writing this, it's 8 a.m. and I'm drinking my third coffee. Wish me luck!

True or false?

1. Lily's friends go to bed later than she does.

2. Lily works from home.

3. She feels most creative in the evening.

4. At the weekend she gets up early.

5. This month she's changing her routine.

6. She's learning Spanish for her job.

Talk: Are you like Lily?

  1. What do you and Lily have in common? What is different?
  2. When is your most productive time of day?
  3. Lily is changing her routine this month. Are you changing anything in your life at the moment?
  4. Would you like Lily's routine? Why or why not?

Grammar detective

Find in the text: 3 things Lily does every day or usually and 3 things that are happening now or this month. Look at the verbs. What's the difference?

Habits or right now?

7 min

Step 1. Look at two sentences from the text and answer the questions.

A. I usually wake up at around ten.
B. This month I'm trying to go to bed earlier.

1. Sentence A: is it a habit, something Lily does again and again?

2. Sentence B: is it Lily's normal routine for always?

3. "I'm drinking my third coffee." When is it happening?

Step 2. Check the rule.

Present Simple

I work · she works · do you work?
  • habits and routines: I usually wake up at ten.
  • facts: My sister lives in Kazan.
  • always, usually, often, sometimes, never, every day, on Mondays

Present Continuous

I'm working · she's working · are you working?
  • right now: I'm drinking my third coffee.
  • temporary, "these days": I'm learning Spanish this month.
  • now, at the moment, today, this week, these days, Look!
Careful! "State" verbs are usually not in Continuous: like, love, hate, want, need, know, understand, believe, remember.
✗ I'm wanting a new phone.   ✓ I want a new phone.

Подсказка. Спросите себя: это обычно / всегда (Simple) или сейчас / в этот период (Continuous)? «Я работаю в банке» = I work. «Я сейчас работаю над проектом» = I'm working.

Step 3. Game: Guess what I'm doing!

Your teacher mimes an action on camera. Ask yes/no questions to guess. Then it's your turn to mime!

Are you cooking?Are you brushing your teeth?Is it a sport?Are you doing it with your hands?

Present Perfect or Past Simple?

10 min

Step 1. Notice. Look at two sentences about the study.

A. The researchers have followed these people since 1938.
B. The study started in 1938.

1. Sentence A: is the study still going on now?

2. Sentence B: do we know exactly when it happened?

3. "I've known Anna for ten years." Do I still know Anna?

4. "I lived in Kazan for five years." Do I live in Kazan now?

Step 2. Check the rule.

Past Simple: finished time

in 1938NOW
V2 / V-ed · did you…?
  • When? We know or ask about the time: The study started in 1938.
  • Stories and details: We met at university.
  • yesterday, last year, in 2015, ago, when I was a child

Present Perfect: past + now

1938NOW
have / has + V3
  • From the past until now: The study has followed them since 1938.
  • Life experience, no exact time: I've been to Italy.
  • Result now: I've lost my keys!
  • ever, never, already, yet, just, for, since

Подсказка. В русском одно прошедшее время, поэтому спросите себя: важно, КОГДА это было (есть «вчера», «в 2015», «неделю назад»)? Тогда Past Simple. Важен опыт или результат к сегодняшнему дню, а точного времени нет? Тогда Present Perfect. Со словом ago Present Perfect не бывает.

Step 3. How real conversations work.

A: Have you ever been to Georgia? (experience: Present Perfect)
B: Yes, I have! (short answer)
A: Really? When did you go? (details: Past Simple)
B: I went there two years ago. The food was amazing!

Step 4. Sort the time words.

  1. yesterday →
  2. ever →
  3. two days ago →
  4. already →
  5. in 2019 →
  6. since Monday →
  7. when I was a child →
  8. yet →

Real or imaginary? Conditionals

8 min

Zero: always true

If + present, present

If a task feels scary, our brain wants to avoid it.

facts, rules, habits (if = when)

First: real future

If + present, will + V

If I finish this today, I'll go out tonight.

a real possibility. Also unless (= if not), when, as soon as + present

Second: imaginary

If + past, would + V

If I didn't procrastinate, I would have much more free time.

unreal now or unlikely future. If I were you, I'd… = advice

The golden rule: no will and no would in the if-part!
✗ If I will have time, I will call you.   ✓ If I have time, I'll call you.
✗ If I would be rich…   ✓ If I were rich…

Подсказка. Русское «если бы» почти всегда переводится вторым типом: «Если бы у меня было время…» = If I had time, I would… Обычное «если» о реальном будущем — первый тип, но после if ставим настоящее время, хотя по-русски там будущее: «Если я закончу…» = If I finish…

Reading: My Week Without a Phone

10 min

My Week Without a Phone

by Alex, 15

Last month my school organised a challenge: no smartphones for seven days. At first I thought it was a terrible idea. I usually spend about five hours a day on my phone, mostly scrolling TikTok and texting my friends.

Day 1 was awful. I kept reaching for my pocket, and I felt like I was missing everything. Classic FOMO! On Day 2 I got bored, so I took out my old guitar and started practising again. By Day 4 I was sleeping better and I wasn't as tired in class.

The strangest thing? I talked to my family much more. My dad and I even cooked dinner together, and it was actually fun.

Of course, it wasn't perfect. I missed a party because nobody could text me about it! But I've learned something important: my phone is useful, but it shouldn't control my day. Now I turn off notifications after 9 p.m., and I've never felt better.

1. What did Alex think about the challenge at first?

2. What did Alex do on Day 2?

3. What changed by Day 4?

4. Why did Alex miss a party?

5. What does Alex do now?

Reading: The Worst (and Best) Trip

10 min

The Worst (and Best) Trip of My Life

a travel story by Kate

Last summer my friend Anya and I flew to Rome. Everything went wrong from the start. While we were waiting at the airport, they announced that our flight was delayed by five hours! We finally arrived at midnight. When we got to the hotel, the receptionist was sleeping, and he wasn't very happy to see us.

The next day we decided to explore the city without a map. Of course, we got lost. It was raining, and we were walking through tiny streets when an old man stopped us. "Are you lost?" he asked with a smile. He didn't speak much English, but he took us to a small family restaurant. While we were eating the best pasta of our lives, his granddaughter was playing the accordion.

We missed half of the sightseeing on our list, but that evening was the best part of the trip. Sometimes the best moments happen when you don't plan them.

True or false?

1. Their flight was delayed.

2. The receptionist was waiting for them with a smile.

3. They had a map.

4. It was sunny when they got lost.

5. An old man helped them.

6. They saw everything on their list.

Look at the story again. Find verbs with was/were + -ing. What were people doing?

Past Simple or Past Continuous?

8 min
we were waiting… (long)they announced (short)

Past Continuous: the background

was / were + V-ing
  • an action in progress: We were walking through tiny streets…
  • the "scene" of a story: It was raining.
  • often after while

Past Simple: the events

V2 / V-ed
  • short, finished actions: An old man stopped us.
  • one action after another: We arrived, went to the hotel and slept.
  • often after when
I / he / she / ityou / we / they
+I was sleepingWe were sleeping
−She wasn't sleepingThey weren't sleeping
?Was he sleeping?Were you sleeping?
Story formula: I was ___ing when something happened.  /  While I was ___ing, something happened.

Подсказка. Past Continuous отвечает на вопрос «что делал?» (процесс, фон). Past Simple отвечает на вопрос «что сделал?» (короткое действие, которое прервало процесс). «Я шла по улице, когда встретила друга» = I was walking down the street when I met a friend.

Talking about the future

10 min
What to do
  1. Read the two predictions and answer the questions about them.
  2. Read the rule and the examples. Say the examples out loud, using the short forms.
  3. Sort the phrases on the probability scale and press «Проверить».
  4. Talk about it: answer the questions using the new forms.
A. This time next year, I'll be studying at university.
B. By 2035, AI will have replaced many office jobs.

1. Sentence A: will the studying be in progress at that moment next year?

2. Sentence B: will the replacing be finished before 2035?

3. "By the time you read this, I will have left." When do I leave?

Future Continuous

will be + V-ing
  • an action in progress at a moment in the future: This time tomorrow I'll be flying to Dubai.
  • polite questions about plans: Will you be using the car tonight?

Future Perfect

will have + V3
  • finished before a moment in the future: By 2030, I'll have graduated.
  • by + time · by the time + present: By the time we arrive, the film will have started.
Say it naturally
In speech we use short forms and the small words are weak: I'll be studying → /aɪl bi/ · I'll have finished → /aɪl əv/ — "have" sounds like "of". Say the examples above quickly, like in a real conversation.
How sure are you?
certain: will definitely · almost certain: is bound to, will probably, is likely to · quite possible: may well · possible: might, could · probably not: is unlikely to, probably won't · impossible: definitely won't

Подсказка. Future Continuous — «буду делать» в конкретный момент будущего (процесс). Future Perfect — «уже сделаю» к моменту в будущем (результат). Слово by («к») почти всегда зовёт Future Perfect.

Sort the phrases

  1. AI is bound to change medicine. →
  2. Robots may well deliver our food. →
  3. People are unlikely to stop using phones. →
  4. Prices will definitely go up. →
  5. Flying cars might appear in cities. →
  6. Books probably won't disappear. →
Talk about it
  • What will you be doing this time next year?
  • What will you have achieved by the time you are 25?
  • Name one thing that is bound to happen in technology in the next five years, and one thing that is unlikely to happen. Does your partner agree?

Give a reason and an example. Then ask your partner a follow-up question: "Why?", "Can you give an example?", "What about you?"

  • What will your phone be able to do in 2035?
Talk about it
  • Which question was the most interesting? Why?
  • Did your partner say anything that surprised you?
  • Which question would you like to ask your friends or family?

Give a reason and an example. Then ask your partner a follow-up question: "Why?", "Can you give an example?", "What about you?"

Debate

15 min
What to do
  1. Choose a motion. One of you argues FOR, the other AGAINST.
  2. Plan: write three arguments with an example for each. Check them: is it a fact or an opinion?
  3. Debate: present your arguments, then argue freely. Use the debate moves. There is no timer.
  4. Report: tell your teacher who was more convincing and why. Then talk about the questions.

1. Choose a motion

Press the button to choose a motion
  • "AI will create more jobs than it destroys."
  • "Children under 14 shouldn't have smartphones."
  • "Social media does more harm than good."
  • "Companies must always tell us when we are talking to an AI."
  • "Self-driving cars should be allowed everywhere."

2. Plan your arguments

Write three arguments and an example for each. Your teacher can see them.

Zakhar
Mikhail
Check your arguments
Is it a fact or an opinion? · What is your evidence or example? · What will the other side say — and how will you answer?

3. Debate

Agree and add: "That's true, and what's more…"Challenge: "But what would happen if…?"Counter-example: "Take … for example."Ask for evidence: "How do you know that?"Concede a point: "Fair enough, but…"
Making your point
I'd argue that…The key point here is…The evidence suggests…Let's not forget that…
Challenging
I see where you're coming from, but…That's a fair point, however…That may be true, but it doesn't mean…What you're missing is…

Final word: sum up your position in one sentence about the future, e.g. "By 2040, AI will have…"

Talk about it
  • Which argument from the other side was the strongest?
  • Did anyone change their mind, even a little? Why?
  • Forget your role: what do you really think about the motion?
  • Which was easier to argue: FOR or AGAINST? Why?

Give a reason and an example. Then ask your partner a follow-up question: "Why?", "Can you give an example?", "What about you?"

4. Bonus, if you have time: startup pitch

Each of you invents an app or a gadget that solves a real problem. Present it. The others are investors: they ask two tough questions and decide whether to invest.

Pitching
Our app will…By 2030, it will have…Users are bound to…What makes it different is…
Investors
Who will be using it?How will you make money?What if a big company copies you?I'm in! / I'm out, because…
Talk about it
  • Would you really invest in your partner's idea? Why or why not?
  • Which problem in your life would you most like an app to solve?

Give a reason and an example. Then ask your partner a follow-up question: "Why?", "Can you give an example?", "What about you?"

Sunday at Grandma's

10 min

a Read the story quickly. What is it mainly about?

Sunday at Grandma'sA reader's story · about 180 words

When I was a child, we used to visit my grandmother every Sunday. She lived in a small house with a big garden, and the whole house used to smell of fresh bread. Grandma didn't use to buy cakes in shops — everything was homemade. In summer we used to pick strawberries in her garden, and she baked the most mouth-watering strawberry pie I have ever tasted.

I remember one Sunday very well. I was eight, and I tried to bake the pie myself. I forgot the sugar! Grandma tasted it, smiled and said, "Well, it's very… healthy." We laughed for hours.

My grandmother died many years ago, but I still have her recipe, written in her small, neat handwriting. Every summer I bake her strawberry pie with my daughter. It never tastes exactly the same, but it always tastes like home.

The story is mainly about…

Olga, 46 an accountant from Kazan

For twenty years I was stuck in a rut: home, office, home. Last year I took a year off and moved to a small village by the sea in Montenegro. I took up painting, and now I sell my pictures to tourists. I don't know if I will go back.

Igor, 52 an engineer

second conditional

12 min

a Real or imagined? Read the examples, then choose for each sentence.

Real, possible
If it rains tomorrow, I'll stay at home.
It can really happen.
Imagined
If I lived by the sea, I'd swim every day.
I don't live by the sea — I'm imagining.
  1. If I have time tonight, I'll call you. →
  2. If I had a year off, I'd travel around Asia. →
  3. If I won a million, I'd buy a house by the sea. →
  4. If you're tired, we'll stop. →

b Read the rules in the Grammar Bank. Remember: in the if-part there is no would.

Grammar Bank1Asecond conditional
IF + past formIf I hadlived · had · were · could
,
would ('d) + verbI would travelwould go · 'd buy · would be

Past form, but not past time! We talk about now or the future — something imagined.

❌ If I would have money, I would travel.
✅ If I had money, I would travel.

Подсказка. В русском «бы» стоит в обеих частях: «Если бы у меня были деньги, я бы путешествовала». В английском would («бы») — только в одной части, а после if — прошедшая форма: If I had… Части можно менять местами: I would travel if I had money. Для всех лиц можно were: If I were you…

Check: "If I had more money, I would buy a car." — Do I have a lot of money now?

Nature's Record-Breakers

12 min

a Before you read: guess! Then read and check.

Which animal travels the furthest every year?

Which tiny animal has survived a trip into space?

Which animal has the strongest bite ever measured?

Which is the heaviest animal that has ever lived?

Nature's Record-BreakersA magazine article · about 280 words

A Every year, the Arctic tern flies from the Arctic to the Antarctic and back again — about 70,000 kilometres. It is one of the longest migrations of any animal on Earth. In its life of around 30 years, an Arctic tern can fly as far as going to the Moon and back three times!

B Tardigrades, or 'water bears', are less than one millimetre long, so a tardigrade isn't as big as an ant — it is much smaller. But it is far tougher. Tardigrades can survive extreme cold and heat, and in 2007 scientists sent some into space. Many of them came back alive.

C The blue whale is not only the biggest animal alive today; it is the heaviest animal that has ever lived. It can be up to 30 metres long and is heavier than 25 elephants. Even a baby blue whale is bigger than most adult animals.

D The saltwater crocodile has the strongest bite ever measured in a living animal. Its bite is far stronger than a lion's or a tiger's. Luckily, the muscles that open its jaws are quite weak.

E Sloths spend most of their lives in trees and come down only about once a week — to go to the toilet! They move so slowly that tiny plants called algae grow on their fur, which gives them green camouflage. For a sloth, the slower it moves, the less energy it uses.

comparatives and superlatives: going further

12 min

a Look at the article again. Find and underline (say to your teacher) one example of each:

  1. much / far + comparative
  2. not as … as
  3. the + superlative + ever
  4. one of the + superlative
  5. the …, the …

b Read the rules in the Grammar Bank. Then do the exercises — this time you write the answers!

Grammar Bank1Acomparatives and superlatives
ruleexample
much / far / a bit + comparativeA tardigrade is much smaller than an ant. Its bite is far stronger. I'm a bit taller than my sister.
(not) as … asA tardigrade isn't as big as an ant. My cat is as lazy as a sloth!
the + superlative + (that) … everthe heaviest animal that has ever lived · the best film I've ever seen
one of the + superlative + plural nounIt is one of the longest migrations on Earth.
less / the leastSharks are less dangerous than people think. It's the least interesting fact.
the + comparative, the + comparativeThe slower it moves, the less energy it uses. The bigger, the better!

Подсказка. much / far = «намного», a bit = «чуть-чуть»: much faster — намного быстрее (но не very faster!). not as … as = «не такой …, как». После one of the — всегда множественное число: one of the best players. The …, the … = «чем …, тем …».

1 Write the correct form of the adjective.

  1. A tardigrade is much (small) than an ant.
  2. The saltwater crocodile has one of the (strong) bites in the world.
  3. My cat is a bit (lazy) than my dog.
  4. This is the (good) documentary I've ever seen!
  5. Yesterday's test was far (bad) than today's.
  6. The (far) you walk, the (tired) you get.

2 Complete the second sentence so it means the same.

  1. A horse is slower than a cheetah.
    A horse isn't a cheetah.
  2. A mouse is lighter than a cat.
    A mouse isn't a cat.
  3. I have never seen such a beautiful bird.
    It's the I've ever seen.
  4. Bees and ants are both very hard-working.
    Bees are ants.
  5. When it moves more slowly, a sloth uses less energy.
    The a sloth moves, the energy it uses.

Plan B: when things go wrong

10 min

a Read three stories. Which plan B was the best?

The festival Max, 24

We were looking forward to the music festival for months. The day before, they called it off because of a storm. We were so disappointed! But my friend came up with a plan B: we set up a mini festival in his garden with a speaker and a barbecue. Twenty people turned up. Honestly, it was better than the real one.

The road trip Dasha, 31

We set off for the mountains at six in the morning. Three hours later we ran out of petrol — the nearest station was 20 km away. A farmer stopped and gave us some petrol from his tractor. Next time I will check everything before we leave!

The flight Ilya, 27

My flight was cancelled and the next one was in two days. I couldn't put off the business meeting, so I figured out a route by train and bus. It took 19 hours, but I arrived just in time. As soon as I walked in, my boss said, "Why do you look so tired?"

  2. Max enjoyed the garden party less than a real festival. →
  3. Dasha was driving the car. →
  4. They got petrol from a farmer. →
  5. Ilya's meeting was put off. →
  6. Ilya travelled for almost a day. →

first conditional and future time clauses

12 min

a Look at these sentences. What tense comes after if, when and as soon as?

If the festival is cancelled, we'll have a party in the garden.

After if / when / as soon as / until we use…

b Read the rules in the Grammar Bank. Then do the exercises.

Grammar Bank1Bfirst conditional; future time clauses
if / when / as soon as / until / before / after + present simpleWhen I arriveif it rains · as soon as I know · until he calls
,
will / won't + verbI'll call youwe'll stay · I won't go

Future meaning, but after if, when, as soon as, until, before, after, unless we use the present simple!

wordmeaningexample
ifmaybe it will happenIf the flight is cancelled, I'll take the train.
whenI'm sure it will happenWhen I get home, I'll text you.
unless= if … notWe'll miss the train unless we leave now.
as soon asimmediately whenI'll call you as soon as I land.
untilup to the time whenI'll wait until you come.
❌ When I will arrive, I'll call you.
❌ If it will rain, we'll stay home.
✅ When I arrive, I'll call you.
✅ If it rains, we'll stay home.

Подсказка. В русском после «когда / если» будущее: «когда приеду, позвоню». В английском после when / if / as soon as / until — настоящее время: when I arrive. will — только в другой части предложения.

there is / there are — Grammar Easy

12 min

a Read the four steps. Press 🔊 and repeat the examples.Прочитайте четыре шага. Нажмите 🔊 и повторите примеры.

Grammar Easy · Грамматика без страхаthere is / there are
1
Одна мысль

Когда мы говорим, что где-то ЕСТЬ, мы начинаем предложение с There is (одна вещь) или There are (много вещей). По-русски: «На моей улице есть кафе» = There is a café in my street. Порядок слов: сначала There is / There are, потом что, потом где.

2
Формула-конструктор
There is+a café+in my street.
There are+two parks+in my town.

Одна вещь → There is (коротко: There's). Две и больше → There are.

There isn't+a cinema.
Is there+a park?+— Yes, there is. / No, there isn't.
3
Смотри, как это работает · нажми 🔊
  • There is a café in my street.
  • There's a big park near my flat.
  • There are three museums in the centre.
  • There isn't a cinema.
  • Is there a pharmacy near here?
4
Осторожно!
❌ There is two parks. → ✅ There are two parks.
Две вещи → are.
❌ In my street is a café. → ✅ There is a café in my street.
Начинаем с There is.
❌ There are a café. → ✅ There is a café.
a = одна → is.

A Great Weekend

Learn to listen like a pro: 5 simple rules, two listening tasks, weekend words and the Past Simple -ed — the easy way.

“We have two ears and one mouth so that we can listen twice as much as we speak.”Epictetus
A2WeekendsPast Simple -edListening skills60 min
ListeningVocabularyGrammarPronunciationListeningSpeakingWritingFeedbackHomework: wordsHomework: grammar

the main idea

10 min
In this lesson you will…
  • use 5 rules to listen betterнаучитесь слушать по 5 правилам
  • understand people talking about their weekendпонимать рассказы о выходных
  • use the Past Simple: I watched, I playedговорить в прошедшем времени
  • pronounce -ed endingsправильно произносить окончание -ed
How to listen · Как слушать (5 правил)
  1. Predict. Сначала посмотрите на картинки и вопросы — угадайте, о чём будет текст.
  2. Main idea first. В первый раз слушайте только общий смысл. Не нужно понимать каждое слово!
  3. Key words. Во второй раз ищите ключевые слова: кто? что? где? когда?
  4. Numbers. Числа и время записывайте цифрами сразу: 7.30, 15, 42.
  5. Transcript last. Текст открывайте только в конце — и слушайте ещё раз, следя по тексту.

a Rule 1 · Predict. Look at the pictures. Mia and Ben talk about their weekend. Who did what, do you think?Посмотрите на картинки и угадайте, кто что делал.

b Rule 2 · Main idea. Listen once. Don't read! Answer one question.Послушайте один раз без текста и ответьте на один вопрос.

Mia and Ben: Monday morningListen for the main idea · Общий смысл
  1. Ben:Hi Mia! How was your weekend?
  2. Mia:Oh, it was great, thanks! On Saturday I visited my grandparents in the country.
  3. Ben:Nice! What did you do there?
  4. Mia:We walked in the forest, and my grandma and I baked an apple cake. It was delicious!
  5. Ben:Lucky you! My weekend was really boring.
  6. Mia:Why? What happened?
  7. Ben:It rained all weekend, so I stayed at home. I cleaned my flat and I watched three films.
  8. Mia:That's not boring! Which films?
  9. Ben:Old comedies. And on Sunday I played computer games with my brother till midnight.
  10. Mia:Ha! I didn't watch any films. I listened to music on the train and I was in bed at ten.

Who had a better weekend?

c Rule 3 · Key words. Listen again. Who did it — Mia or Ben?Послушайте ещё раз. Кто это делал — Миа или Бен?

  1. visited grandparents →
  2. baked a cake →

1
Одна мысль

Когда мы рассказываем о том, что уже было (вчера, в выходные, в прошлом году), мы просто добавляем к глаголу -ed. Для всех одинаково: I, you, he, she, we, they — watched. Никаких was, никаких -s!

2
Формула-конструктор
I+watched+a film+yesterday.
She+played+tennis+last weekend.

Нет → didn't + глагол без -ed:

I+didn't+watch+TV.
Did+you+watch+TV?+— Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.
3

4
Осторожно!
❌ Yesterday I watch a film. → ✅ Yesterday I watched a film.
Прошлое → добавляем -ed.
❌ I was watched TV. → ✅ I watched TV.
Was не нужен!
❌ I didn't watched TV. → ✅ I didn't watch TV.
После didn't — без -ed.

  9. Ellie:Is there anything you miss?
  10. Gran (Margaret):I miss the slower pace of life. But I certainly don't miss washing clothes by hand!
  11. Ellie:And was anything difficult to get used to?
  12. Gran (Margaret):Mobile phones! I'm still getting used to texting. Your messages are so short — I never know if you're angry with me!

used to / would; be used to / get used to

14 min

a Read the Grammar Bank.

Grammar Bank1Aused to · would · be / get used to
past habits and statesexample
+used to + verbI used to walk to school. · I used to have long hair.
–didn't use to + verbWe didn't use to have a phone.
?Did you use to + verb?Did you use to write letters?
+would + verb (only actions!)Every summer we would go to the dacha.
  • would — only for repeated actions, not states: ✗ I would have long hair. ✓ I used to have long hair.
  • After didn't and Did → use to (no -d).
  • be used to + noun / -ing = it's normal for me now: I'm used to getting up early.
  • get used to + noun / -ing = it's becoming normal: I'm getting used to driving on the left.

Подсказка. used to = «раньше (бывало)…», а сейчас уже нет. be used to = «привык», get used to = «привыкать». После be/get used to — существительное или глагол с -ing.

  1. I have long hair when I was a teenager.
  2. Every summer we go to my grandparents' village.
  3. We have a computer at home.
  4. you use to like school?
  5. There be a cinema in our street, but now it's a supermarket.
  6. My dad tell us a story every night.

b be used to or get used to? Tap the right form.

  1. I've lived in London for ten years, so I'm used to in the rain.
  2. It took me months to used to the food.
  3. She isn't used to up so early.
  4. Are you used to your new job yet?

Getting used to Edinburgh

10 min

a Read the article. What surprised Anna most when she moved?

Getting used to Edinburghby Anna, 34, who moved from Kazan to Scotland two years ago · about 250 words

When I moved from Kazan to Edinburgh, I thought the hardest thing would be the language. I was wrong. My English was fine — it was the little things that surprised me.

In Kazan I used to go shopping at any time, even at midnight. Here most shops close at six, and on Sundays the city feels asleep. At first it drove me crazy. Now I plan my week, and I actually like the quiet Sundays.

The weather was the next shock. I used to think Russians were experts in bad weather, but Scottish rain is different: it comes sideways and changes four times a day. I've never got used to it, but I've stopped carrying an umbrella — everyone here just wears a good jacket.

What I love is how people talk to strangers. On the bus the driver calls me "love", and people say "cheers" instead of "thank you". In my first months I would answer with a very formal "You're welcome", and people would smile kindly.

Do I miss home? Of course. I miss my mum's pies and long summer evenings at the dacha. But I'm getting used to my new life, and Edinburgh is slowly becoming home.

1. What was the biggest surprise for Anna?

2. How does she feel about Sundays now?

3. What has she stopped doing?

4. How did people react to her formal "You're welcome"?

Emma's blog

10 min

a Now read Emma's blog. Find five phrases from the Vocabulary Bank. Tap any word you don't know.

Emma's blog · «A week in my life»

Hi, I'm Emma. I'm 27 and I work at a small travel agency in Brighton. My week is usually very simple. I get up at seven, go for a run by the sea and take the bus to work. I finish at five, and I usually do the shopping on the way home. On Fridays I catch up with friends, and on Saturdays I always have a lie-in — I never get up before ten!

But this week is different. My boss is on holiday, so I'm working from home and I'm doing her job too! I'm not going for a run in the mornings because I'm always running late. And this month I'm learning to cook Thai food — I'm taking an online course. It's hard, but I love it.

Next Saturday is my day off… and I've got big plans. More about that tomorrow!

  2. She usually takes the bus to work. →
  3. On Fridays she does the shopping. →
  4. This week she is working in the office. →
  5. She is taking an online cooking course. →
  6. Her day off is next Sunday. →

c Look at the blog again. Is each sentence about Emma's usual week or about this week / now? This is the grammar of the next stage.Обычная неделя или «сейчас / на этой неделе»?

  1. I get up at seven. →
  2. I'm working from home. →
  3. I usually do the shopping on the way home. →
  4. I'm not going for a run in the mornings. →
  5. I never get up before ten. →
  6. I'm learning to cook Thai food. →

present simple vs continuous

15 min

a Read the Grammar Bank. All the examples are from Emma's blog.

Grammar Bank2Apresent simple vs present continuous
present simplepresent continuous
usehabits, routines, facts — usuallynow, this week, temporary situations
+She gets up at seven.She's working from home this week.
–She doesn't work on Saturdays.She's not going for a run this week.
?Does she work on Fridays?What is she doing at the moment?
time wordsusually, always, often, never, every day, on Fridaysnow, at the moment, today, this week, this month, these days
  • He / she / it: -s in the present simple: she gets, he catches, she does.
  • State verbs are not used with -ing: like, love, want, need, know, understand. ✗ I'm loving it ✓ I love it.

Подсказка. «Обычно, всегда, по пятницам» → present simple. «Сейчас, на этой неделе, в этом месяце» → present continuous.

  1. Emma usually at seven.
  2. This week she from home.
  3. She the shopping on the way home every day.
  4. At the moment she an online course.
  5. On Saturdays she always a lie-in.
  6. She Thai food — it's delicious!

future forms

15 min

a Read the Grammar Bank. The examples are from Emma's phone call.

Grammar Bank2Afuture: present continuous · going to · will
formwhen?example
present continuousarrangement: the time, place, people or tickets are fixedI'm meeting my sister at nine. We're taking the ten o'clock train.
be going toplan, intention — you decided beforeWe're going to walk by the river.
be going toprediction — you can see it nowLook at the sky! It's going to rain.
willdecision now · offer · promiseThen I'll take my umbrella. I'll bring a cake.
willopinion about the future: I think…, probablyI think you'll love Oxford.

Подсказка. Есть время, билеты, договорённость → I'm meeting. Решили заранее → I'm going to. Решаете прямо сейчас, предлагаете, обещаете → I'll.

unusual jobs

10 min

a Listen to Jess and Max. Which job would you prefer?

Radio: «Work Talk»Listen first · Text at the end
  1. Host:Today on «Work Talk» we meet two people with very unusual jobs. Jess, you're a zookeeper. What's a normal day like?
  2. Jess, zookeeper:There's no normal day! I have to start at seven, because the animals have to eat early. I clean, I feed, I check that everyone is healthy.
  3. Host:Is it dangerous?
  4. Jess, zookeeper:Sometimes. We mustn't go into the big cats' area alone — never. And you have to be fit: I walk about fifteen kilometres a day.
  5. Host:Max, you test hotels. That sounds like a dream job!
  6. Max, hotel tester:Everybody says that! I stay in a different hotel every few nights. I have to check everything: the bed, the shower, the breakfast, even how fast they answer the phone.
  7. Host:Do you have to tell them who you are?
  8. Max, hotel tester:No, I mustn't! It's a secret. And I don't have to pay — the company pays. But I write a long report every night, and I don't see my family much.
  9. Host:Any advice for people who want your jobs?
  10. Jess, zookeeper:You should volunteer at a farm or a zoo first. You'll know very quickly if it's for you.
  11. Max, hotel tester:And you should really like being alone. Hotels can be lonely places!

must, have to, should

14 min

a Read the Grammar Bank.

Grammar Bank1Bmust · have to · don't have to · mustn't · should
meaningexample
have to / mustit's necessary (a rule)Zookeepers have to start early. You must wear a helmet.
don't have toit isn't necessary (you can if you want)Max doesn't have to pay for hotels.
mustn'tit's forbidden — don't do it!You mustn't tell the hotel who you are.
should / shouldn'tadvice — a good ideaYou should volunteer first.
  • Past: had to (✗ musted): I had to work late yesterday.
  • Questions: Do you have to wear a uniform? Does she have to…?

Осторожно! don't have to = «не обязательно», а mustn't = «нельзя». Это совсем разные вещи!

  1. You use your phone while driving. It's dangerous!
  2. It's Saturday — I get up early.
  3. Doctors study for many years.
  4. You look tired. You go to bed earlier.
  5. you have to wear a uniform at work?
  6. Yesterday I stay at work until nine.

b don't have to or mustn't? Write the answer.

  1. In my office we wear a suit — jeans are fine.
  2. You smoke in the hospital.
  3. Students copy in exams.
  4. She works from home, so she travel to work.

d Look: Daniel says I teach, but we say he teaches. Why? That's the grammar of the next stage.Дэниел говорит I teach, а мы о нём — he teaches. Почему? Это грамматика следующего этапа.

present simple: he / she

15 min

a Read the four steps. Press 🔊 and repeat. All the examples are about Daniel.Прочитайте четыре шага. Нажмите 🔊 и повторите. Все примеры — про Дэниела.

Grammar Easy · Грамматика без страхаhe / she + -s
1
Одна мысль

Когда говорим о нём или о ней (he, she, it, Daniel, my wife), к глаголу добавляем -s. I teach → he teaches. А «не» для него/неё — doesn't, и тогда -s уже не нужно: he doesn't teach.

2
Формула-конструктор
I+teach+Russian.
He+teaches+Russian.

+s: gets, starts · +es (после ch, sh, o): teaches, watches, goes, does · y → ies: studies · have → has

I+don't+give+tests.
She+doesn't+give+tests.
3
Смотри, как это работает · нажми 🔊
  • Daniel teaches Russian.
  • He goes to school by bike.
  • He has a coffee at break.
  • His wife works in a hospital.
  • He doesn't give a lot of tests.
4
Осторожно!
❌ He teach Russian. → ✅ He teaches Russian.
он / она → -s
❌ She don't work. → ✅ She doesn't work.
он / она → doesn't
❌ He doesn't teaches. → ✅ He doesn't teach.
после doesn't — без -s

  2. «I teach five lessons a day.» → He five lessons a day.
  3. «I go to school by bike.» → He to school by bike.
  4. «I have a coffee at break.» → He a coffee at break.
  5. «I check homework after lessons.» → He homework after lessons.
  6. «I don't give a lot of tests.» → He a lot of tests.

  6. prepare → she
  7. do → she
  8. explain → she

  1. Daniel speak Russian at home.

c Open the transcript. Find the questions. They start with Do or Does. When do we use Does? That's the next grammar.Откройте текст. Вопросы начинаются с Do или Does. Когда Does? Это следующая грамматика.

questions: Do / Does

12 min

a Read the four steps. Press 🔊 and repeat the questions from the interview.Прочитайте четыре шага. Повторите вопросы из интервью.

Grammar Easy · Грамматика без страхаDo you…? Does he…?
1
Одна мысль

В вопросе в начало ставим помощника: Do (I, you, we, they) или Does (he, she, it). Глагол — без -s: Does he teach? Короткий ответ повторяет помощника: Yes, he does. / No, he doesn't.

2
Формула-конструктор
Do+you+give+homework?
Does+he+give+homework?

Ответ: Yes, I do. / No, I don't. · Yes, he does. / No, he doesn't. — не просто «Yes».

What time+do+you+get up?
Where+does+she+work?
3
Смотри, как это работает · нажми 🔊
  • Do you speak Russian at home?
  • Does your wife like Russian food? — Yes, she does.
  • What time do you get up?
  • Does your cat speak Russian? — No, it doesn't.
4
Осторожно!
❌ Does he teaches? → ✅ Does he teach?
после does — без -s
❌ You like tests? → ✅ Do you like tests?
в начале — Do
❌ Do she work? → ✅ Does she work?
she → Does

Grammar Bank1Bpast simple and past continuous
was walking along the beach (long action, background)

past continuous: was / were + -ingpast simple

when + past simple (short action) · while + past continuous (long action): I was carrying the cake when the dog ran under my feet. While I was living in London, I met her.

The call from "IT Support"

12 min

a Read the case study. In one sentence: how did the attack work?

The Call from "IT Support"A case study · about 300 words

At 4.45 on a Friday afternoon, Maria, an accountant at a mid-sized logistics company, received a call. "Hi Maria, it's Alex from IT support. We're seeing some strange activity on your account — it looks like someone in another country is trying to log in. I need to verify a few things quickly before the weekend."

Alex sounded friendly and professional. He knew Maria's full name, her manager's name and the name of the accounting software she used every day. He asked her to read out the six-digit code that had just arrived on her phone, "to confirm it's really you". Maria hesitated for a second, then read out the code. Alex thanked her and wished her a nice weekend.

On Monday morning, the finance director discovered that three payments, worth almost €90,000 in total, had been sent to an unknown bank account over the weekend. There was no Alex in the IT department.

The investigation showed that the attacker hadn't used any sophisticated malware. He had found most of the information on the company website and on social media. Maria's team page listed her role, and her manager had posted about the new accounting software on a professional network. The six-digit code was the second factor of her two-factor authentication — the one thing that should have protected her.

"People think hacking is about code," says the security consultant who led the investigation. "But most attacks start with a conversation. The attacker doesn't break in — he's invited in."

The attack mainly worked because…

  6. The company got the money back. →

modals of deduction: present and past

12 min

a Read the investigator's notes. How sure is she in each sentence?

b Read the rules in the Grammar Bank. Then do the exercises.

Grammar Bank1Amodals of deduction
how sure?presentpast
✅ I'm sure it's trueHe must be an insider.He must have known her name.
🤔 It's possibleIt might / may / could be a test.He might / may / could have found it online.
❌ I'm sure it's not trueIt can't be a mistake.It can't / couldn't have been a random call.

Past deduction: modal + have + past participle (must have sent, might have seen, can't have known).

❌ He mustn't have known. (= opposite of must for deduction)
❌ He must has known.
✅ He can't have known.
✅ He must have known.

Подсказка. must have done = «наверняка сделал», might / could have done = «возможно, сделал», can't have done = «не мог сделать». Для «точно нет» используем can't, а не mustn't.

    He her on LinkedIn.

    It a technical problem.

    They our network now.

Grammar Bank1Acan / can't
✅ can + verb

I can't sing.
He can't skate.
They can't draw.
? Can you swim? — Yes, I can. / No, I can't.

Risky Business

B2Risk & decisionsThird conditionalStorytelling60–65 min

risk and decisions

12 min
In this lesson you will…
  • use natural phrases about risk and decisions
  • talk about past situations that didn't happen with the third conditional
  • express regrets with I wish / If only
  • tell the story of a turning point in your life

a How risky is it? Rate each picture from 1 (safe) to 5 (very risky). Explain your rating.

Talk about it
  • Which would you never do? Why?
  • Are you a risk-taker or do you usually play it safe?

b Go to the Vocabulary Bank. Tap each card, press 🔊 and repeat. Then complete the sentences.

Vocabulary Bank1ARisk and decisions
  1. Learning to dive really made me step out of my comfort .
  2. He was so — he drove at 180 km/h in the rain.
  3. Moving to St Petersburg was a turning in my career.
  4. I was about to sign the contract, but then I had second .
  5. Our plan to save time : the project took twice as long.
  6. Years of practice finally — she won the competition.

c Discuss.

Talk about it
  • What is the biggest risk you have ever taken? Did it pay off?
  • Are people more cautious or more reckless as they get older? Why?
  • When is it smart to play it safe?

Give a reason and an example. Then ask a follow-up question: "Why?", "What about you?"

Turning points

10 min

a Read three stories. Which decision paid off? Which backfired?

Pavel, 38

Ten years ago I had a safe job in a bank. Then a friend asked me to join his tiny start-up. Everyone told me to play it safe, but I went for it. For two years we earned almost nothing. Then a large company bought us. If I hadn't taken that risk, I would still be counting other people's money.

Lena, 45

I invested all my savings in a friend's restaurant. I had second thoughts, but I didn't want to let her down. The restaurant closed after eight months and I lost everything. I wish I had listened to my sister. In hindsight, it was a gamble, not an investment.

Artem, 29

I almost didn't go to my friend's birthday party — I was tired and wanted to stay at home. At the last minute I changed my mind. That night I met Katya. We've been married for three years now. If I had stayed at home, we would never have met.

b Who…? Choose the name.

  1. …didn't follow other people's advice? →
  2. …regrets a decision? →
  3. …made a decision at the last minute? →
  4. …had very little money for a while? →
  5. …lost money because of loyalty to a friend? →
  6. …met someone important by chance? →

c Discuss.

Talk about it
  • Whose story is the most surprising?
  • Was Lena wrong to help her friend?
  • Is luck more important than good decisions?

Give a reason and an example. Then ask a follow-up question: "Why?", "What about you?"

third conditional; wish / if only

12 min

a Find in the stories: one third conditional and one sentence with wish. Did these things happen?

"If I had stayed at home, we would never have met." — Did Artem stay at home?

"I wish I had listened to my sister." — Did Lena listen to her sister?

b Read the rules in the Grammar Bank. Then do the exercises.

Grammar Bank1Athird conditional; wish / if only
IF + past perfectIf I had knownhad gone · hadn't stayed · had listened
,
would have + past participleI would have helpedwould have met · wouldn't have lost

An imagined past: it didn't happen, and we can't change it.

regret about…structureexample
the pastI wish / If only + past perfectI wish I had listened to my sister. If only I hadn't invested!
the presentI wish / If only + past simpleI wish I had more time. (= I don't have it now)
❌ If I would have known, I would have helped.
❌ I wish I didn't invest last year.
✅ If I had known, I would have helped.
✅ I wish I hadn't invested last year.

Подсказка. Третье условное — о прошлом, которого не было: «если бы я тогда знал, я бы помог». В части с if — had + V3, в другой — would have + V3. I wish + had done = «жаль, что не сделал / как жаль, что сделал».

1 Choose the correct form.

  1. If we earlier, we wouldn't have missed the flight.
  2. She the job if she had prepared better.
  3. I wish I that to my boss yesterday.
  4. If only I more free time now!
  5. If he so reckless, he wouldn't have crashed.

2 Rewrite the sentences.

  1. I didn't know about the sale, so I didn't buy the TV.
    If I about the sale, I the TV.
  2. I regret quitting my job.
    I wish I my job.
  3. He didn't take the risk, so he didn't become rich.
    If he the risk, he rich.
  4. It's a pity I don't speak Spanish.
    I wish I Spanish.

talking about your job

In this lesson you will…

a Fluent is great — now let's make it accurate. Answer the questions in 2–3 sentences. Your teacher writes down your mistakes for «Fix my English».

a warehouse tour

a Kate shows a visitor around an automated distribution centre. Listen once. Put the stages in order.

A tour of a distribution centreListen first · Text at the end
  1. Kate (warehouse manager):Welcome to our distribution centre! Let me show you how it works. First, the trucks arrive at the loading dock.
  2. Mark (visitor):How many trucks do you get a day?
  3. Kate (warehouse manager):About forty. The goods are unloaded and every pallet is scanned, so the system knows exactly what has arrived.
  4. Mark (visitor):And then?
  5. Kate (warehouse manager):Then the goods are put away. Ten years ago people did it with forklifts. Now autonomous robots move the shelves to the storage area.
  6. Mark (visitor):Do the robots work all the time?
  7. Kate (warehouse manager):Almost. They work twenty hours a day. When the battery is low, a robot goes to the charging station by itself.
  8. Mark (visitor):That's impressive. What happens when an order comes in?
  9. Kate (warehouse manager):The robot brings the shelf to a picker. The picker takes the item, and a light shows the right box. After that, the order is packed and labelled.
  10. Mark (visitor):So people still pick the items?
  11. Kate (warehouse manager):Yes. Robots are great at moving things, but people are still better at picking different products. Finally, the parcels are loaded onto trucks and shipped.
  12. Mark (visitor):And what was the biggest change after automation?
  13. Kate (warehouse manager):Speed. Before, we processed five thousand orders a day. Now we process twelve thousand — with the same number of people.

present perfect — Grammar Easy

12 min

a Read the four steps. Press 🔊 and repeat.

Grammar Easy · Грамматика без страхаpresent perfect: experiences
1
Одна мысль

Когда мы говорим об опыте за всю жизнь и не говорим когда, используем have / has + V3. Это как «у меня есть такой опыт»: I've been to Italy = «Я бывала в Италии (когда-то)». ever = «когда-нибудь», never = «никогда».

2
Формула-конструктор
I've+been+to Italy.
She's+tried+sushi.
I've+never+seen+a volcano.

I / you / we / they → have ('ve). He / she / it → has ('s). Вопрос:

Have you+ever+been+to Paris?+— Yes, I have. / No, I haven't.

Сказали когда (in June, last year, yesterday)? → это уже Past Simple: I did it in June.

3
Смотри, как это работает · нажми 🔊
  • I've travelled to six countries.
  • My sister has tried sushi.
  • I've never seen a volcano.
  • Have you ever sung karaoke?
  • Yes, I have. I did it in June.
4
Осторожно!
❌ I have been in Paris last year. → ✅ I went to Paris last year.
Есть «когда» → Past Simple.
❌ She have tried it. → ✅ She has tried it.
she → has.
❌ Have you ever saw it? → ✅ Have you ever seen it?
Нужна V3, а не V2.

  10. Lucy:I've never been diving. I'm afraid of deep water. Maybe next year!
  11. Host:What have you learned from the challenge?
  12. Lucy:That I'm braver than I think. And that new experiences make you happy.

from lawyer to baker

10 min

a Listen to Claire. Why did she leave law, and does she regret it?

Podcast: «Second Acts»Listen first · Text at the end
  1. Host:Claire, you spent fifteen years as a lawyer in London. Now you run a bakery in Bath. What happened?
  2. Claire:Burnout, mostly. I remember sitting in the office at midnight and thinking: I can't imagine doing this for another twenty years.
  3. Host:So you just quit?
  4. Claire:Not at once. I'd always enjoyed baking, so I started going to evening classes. I tried selling bread at a local market — just to see what would happen.
  5. Host:And people bought it?

Grammar Bank1Averb + -ing · verb + to · both
patterncommon verbsexample
verb + -ingenjoy, avoid, mind, can't stand, finish, keep, give up, consider, imagine, miss, suggest, riskShe enjoys baking. I can't imagine doing this forever.
verb + todecide, hope, manage, plan, offer, refuse, afford, seem, tend, learn, agree, promiseShe decided to take the plunge.

Verbs that change meaning

verb+ -ing+ to
remember / forgeta memory: I remember sitting there at midnight.a task: Remember to call the bank!
stopquit an activity: Stop waiting.pause to do sth: I stopped to buy bread.
tryan experiment: I tried selling bread at a market.make an effort: I tried to open the door, but it was locked.
regretthe past: I regret not doing it sooner.bad news: We regret to inform you…
go oncontinue the same: He went on working.move to sth new: She went on to become a judge.
meaninvolve: It meant taking a pay cut.intend: I didn't mean to upset you.

an expert interview

a Listen to Dr Hart, a psychologist. According to her, what persuades us more than facts?

Podcast: «Mind Matters»Listen first · Text at the end
  1. Host:Dr Hart, you study why intelligent people believe things that simply aren't true. Where do we even start?
  2. Dr Amelia Hart:With the uncomfortable fact that our brains aren't designed to find the truth. What they're designed to do is protect our sense of who we are.
  3. Host:So when we see a fact that contradicts our beliefs…
  4. Dr Amelia Hart:…we often dig in. It's not the fact itself that persuades us, it's who tells it to us. If someone from 'our side' shares it, we accept it almost instantly.
  5. Host:And social media makes that worse?
  6. Dr Amelia Hart:Considerably. Not only do algorithms show us more of what we already like, but they also reward outrage. Rarely does a calm, nuanced post go viral.
  7. Host:Is there anything we can actually do?
  8. Dr Amelia Hart:Slow down. The thing that protects people most is a simple pause — asking 'How do I know this?' before sharing. Only when we feel a strong emotion should we be especially suspicious.
  9. Host:Have you ever fallen for something yourself?
  10. Dr Amelia Hart:Of course! Never have I felt so foolish as when I shared a 'study' that turned out to be satire. What I learned is that nobody is immune — especially experts.

What persuades us more than the fact itself?

The facts that make us dig in

12 min

a Read the article. Match the headings to paragraphs A–D.

The facts that make us dig inA feature article · about 320 words

A In 2010, two political scientists published a study that would make fact-checkers everywhere uneasy. They showed people a misleading news story, followed by a correction. What they found was startling: for some readers, the correction did not weaken the false belief — it strengthened it. They called it the backfire effect.

B The finding spread fast, partly because it confirmed what many already suspected about human stubbornness. Ironically, it was precisely this kind of appealing, simple story that later researchers began to question. When the experiments were repeated on a much larger scale, the backfire effect almost disappeared. Most people, it turned out, did update their beliefs when shown compelling evidence — just slightly, and rarely as much as the evidence justified.

C So why does it feel as if facts never change anyone's mind? Part of the answer lies in what happens next. People may accept a correction in the moment, but within weeks they drift back to the original belief, especially if it fits their identity. Not only do we remember the myth better than the correction, but repeating the myth in order to debunk it can make it more familiar — and familiarity feels like truth.

D The most effective strategy, researchers now suggest, is not to bombard people with data. It is to offer an alternative explanation, to avoid humiliating them, and — perhaps most importantly — to let the message come from someone they already trust. Facts matter, but the messenger matters almost as much.

  1. Paragraph A →
  2. Paragraph B →
  3. Paragraph C →
  4. Paragraph D →

emphasis: cleft sentences and inversion

14 min

a Read the Grammar Bank.

Grammar Bank1Acleft sentences · negative inversion
structureneutralemphatic
What … is / wasThe pause protects us.What protects us is a simple pause.
It is / was … that / whoThe messenger persuades us.It's the messenger that persuades us.
The thing / reason / place … isI don't understand why people share it.The thing I don't understand is why people share it.
All … is / wasI only wanted the truth.All I wanted was the truth.
negative adverbialinversion (auxiliary + subject)
Not only … but alsoNot only do algorithms show us what we like, but they also reward outrage.
Rarely / SeldomRarely does a calm post go viral.
Never (before)Never have I felt so foolish.
Only when / Only afterOnly when we feel strong emotion should we be suspicious.
Under no circumstances / At no timeUnder no circumstances should you share it.
No sooner … than · Hardly … whenNo sooner had I shared it than I saw the correction.

Подсказка. Инверсия — как в вопросе: do/does/did, have, can, should + подлежащее. После Only when… инверсия во второй части. Это формальный, «ораторский» стиль — 1–2 раза в эссе или выступлении, не в каждом предложении.

  1. Rarely a fact-check get as many shares as the original lie.
  2. Not only believe the story, but she also shared it with fifty people.
  3. Never seen such an obvious fake.
  4. Only when I checked the source it was satire.
  5. worries me most is how fast these stories spread.
  6. It was the photo convinced everyone.
